data.summary: The three‑week plan front‑loads the weak Unit 2 while still introducing the core concepts of each AP Physics 1 unit. Weeks 1 and 2 build new knowledge with focused practice, and Week 3 is dedicated to mixed review and timed free‑response practice covering all remaining units before the exam.

weeks.focus: Strengthen Unit 2 (Force and Translational Dynamics) and review basic kinematics.
tasks: Watch the live Class 10100 recording, taking notes on free‑body diagrams and Newton's 2nd law.
Do 12 free‑response FRQs on free‑body diagrams and applying F=ma; compare answers to the scoring guide.
Complete 8 practice problems on vectors and displacement (1.1‑1.2).
Create a one‑page summary sheet of Newton's laws with example diagrams.

weeks.focus: Introduce work, energy, momentum, and rotational basics.
tasks: Solve 10 problems on kinetic energy and work (3.1‑3.2).
Do 8 FRQs on conservation of energy (3.4) and momentum (4.3).
Work through 6 rotational‑kinematics questions (5.1) and 6 torque problems (5.3).
Write a brief explanation linking linear and rotational motion (5.2) even though it isn’t a listed topic, to solidify connections.

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice for all remaining units.
tasks: Take a 45‑minute timed practice exam covering Units 6‑8 (mix of multiple‑choice and FRQs).
Review each question, marking errors against the scoring guide.
Do 5 free‑response questions on angular momentum and conservation (6.4).
Complete 6 SHM problems (7.1, 7.3) and 4 fluid‑pressure questions (8.2, 8.4).
Update the master summary sheet with key formulas from Units 6‑8.

data.final_week_advice: In the last week, focus on speed and accuracy: simulate exam conditions, use your summary sheet for quick formula recall, and identify any lingering weak spots to review briefly before the test.
